title: Masinissa becomes king of Numidia
description: Masinissa, Rome's ally against Carthage, becomes the first king of a united Numidia and rules it for more than fifty years.

title: Jugurtha takes Cirta
description: Jugurtha captures Cirta and kills his rival Adherbal and the Italian traders in the city, which brings Rome into the Jugurthine War.

title: Timgad founded
description: The emperor Trajan founds a colony for army veterans north of the Aurès mountains, and its street grid survives almost complete.

title: Death of Augustine of Hippo
description: The bishop and theologian Augustine, born at Thagaste, dies while the Vandals besiege his city.

title: Battle of Vescera
description: The Berber leader Kusaila ambushes and kills the Arab general Uqba ibn Nafi, which sets back the Arab conquest of the Maghreb.

title: Rustamid imamate founded
description: Ibadi Muslims choose Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam as imam of a state that holds the central Maghreb until 909.

title: Qal'at Bani Hammad founded
description: Hammad ibn Buluggin builds a fortified city in the Hodna mountains that becomes the capital of the Hammadid dynasty.

title: Kingdom of Tlemcen founded
description: Yaghmurasen ibn Zyan declares his independence from the Almohads and founds the Zayyanid kingdom, which lasts three centuries.

title: Spain captures Oran
description: An army led by Pedro Navarro for Cardinal Cisneros takes the port, which Spain holds for most of the next three centuries.

title: Barbarossa brothers take Algiers
description: The corsairs Oruç and Hayreddin Barbarossa seize Algiers, which soon accepts the Ottoman sultan as overlord and becomes the capital of a regency.

title: Charles V fails to take Algiers
description: A storm wrecks much of the emperor's fleet as his army lands, and the retreat leaves Algiers the main corsair port of the Mediterranean.

title: Bombardment of Algiers
description: A British and Dutch fleet under Lord Exmouth shells the city to make the dey free Christian slaves.

title: French capture of Algiers
description: Three weeks after landing at Sidi Fredj a French army enters Algiers and ends Ottoman rule, the start of 132 years of French rule.

title: French storm Constantine
description: At the second attempt French troops take the city of Ahmed Bey, the last Ottoman governor still holding out.

title: Abdelkader surrenders
description: After fifteen years leading the resistance to the French conquest, Emir Abdelkader gives himself up to General Lamoricière.

title: Mokrani Revolt
description: Cheikh Mokrani begins the largest rising against French rule since the conquest, and after its defeat much Kabyle land is confiscated.

title: Sétif and Guelma massacre
description: Police fire on a nationalist march on the day of Germany's surrender, rioters kill settlers, and French forces and militias kill thousands of Algerians in reprisal.

title: Algerian War begins
description: The National Liberation Front attacks police and army posts across the country, the start of the war of independence.

title: Soummam conference
description: Leaders of the National Liberation Front meet in secret in Kabylia and give the movement a political programme and a command structure.

title: Battle of Algiers
description: French paratroopers break the National Liberation Front's bombing network in the capital, using torture on a scale that divides opinion in France.

title: Independence
description: Algeria becomes independent after a referendum, and most of the European settlers leave for France.

title: Boumédiène takes power
description: The defence minister Houari Boumédiène arrests President Ahmed Ben Bella and rules until his death in 1978.

title: Oil and gas nationalised
description: Boumédiène announces that the state is taking a 51 per cent share in the French oil companies, making Sonatrach the centre of the economy.

title: October Riots
description: Young people riot for a week over prices and unemployment, the army kills hundreds, and the government then ends one-party rule.

title: Army cancels the elections
description: With the Islamic Salvation Front about to win a majority in parliament, generals force President Chadli Bendjedid to resign and cancel the vote, which leads to a decade of civil war.

title: Bentalha massacre
description: Armed men kill more than 200 villagers in one night, one of the worst massacres of the civil war.

title: Bouteflika elected president
description: Abdelaziz Bouteflika wins after the six other candidates withdraw, and later that year offers an amnesty that winds down the civil war.

title: In Amenas hostage crisis
description: Militants linked to al-Qaeda seize a gas plant in the Sahara, and at least 39 foreign workers die before the army retakes it four days later.

title: Bouteflika resigns
description: Weeks of peaceful mass protests, known as the Hirak, and pressure from the army make the president step down after twenty years.
